Title: KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLA. -   The Payload is seen inside of the Bay just before the doors are closed for flight at Pad 39A, Kennedy Space Center, Fla.  Discovery, the orbiter for STS-82 mission, is ready for the launch of the second Hubble Space Telescope service mission.  The payload consists of the Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer (NICMOS) that will be installed, Fine Guidance Sensor #1 (FGS-1), and the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) to be installed.  The STS-82 will launch with a crew of seven at 3:54 a.m. EST, Feb. 11, 1997.  The launch window is 65 minutes in duration.  The Mission Commander for STS-82 is Ken Bowersox.  The purpose of the mission is to upgrade the scientific capabilities, service or replace aging components on the Telescope, and provide a reboost to the optimum altitude.
CreditLine: NASA Image and Video Library (public domain)
